CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Stay at the Washington table and keep drafting text, including purchases and a bounded enforcement clause, but do not sign a one-sided package and do not launch a new tariff or non-tariff wave while List 3 remains at 10%. Use purchase volumes (soy, energy, aircraft) as the tradable concession and refuse to gut industrial-policy or SOE tools without a matching, scheduled US tariff rollback. Keep the Meng/Huawei file legally and diplomatically separate from the trade text so a criminal case cannot be used as last-minute leverage.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not existential. Combined US Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B (List 1–2 at 25%, List 3 at 10% since 2018-09-24), Huawei/Meng remain under US criminal and extradition pressure (DOJ charges unsealed 2019-01-28; Canada advancing extradition), and the real economy is showing the hit: Jan–Feb industrial output +5.3% y/y (17-year low), official manufacturing PMI contracted in February for the first time since Jan 2009, February exports fell the most in three years, the survey jobless rate rose to 5.3% from 4.9%, industrial profits posted their sharpest contraction in a decade, and US customs imports from China dropped ~25% from Nov 2018 to early 2019. That maps below the +0.5 CHN anchor because FX is not in distress (CNY near 6.71/–USD in March, not a reserve-drain crisis) and the most dangerous step—the scheduled List 3 hike from 10% to 25%—has been suspended twice (G20 90-day window; Trump delay on 2019-02-24). Action should therefore be mild, not escalatory: a new Chinese tariff or detention wave would give Washington a pretext to restore the 25% hike and expand lists, while unilateral purchase or structural concessions would be pocketed (Trump has already said he wants to keep the 25% on the original $50B). Intensive talks on 2019-04-03 reported progress on text, including enforcement language, with no deal signed—the correct band is negotiate/hold, not concede_purchases or rollback. Explore de-escalation; do not pre-commit.
key_factors: Existing US tariffs already cover ~$250B of Chinese exports; List 3 hike to 25% is paused but not cancelled
Huawei/Meng criminal-extradition track is a separate, high-salience threat to a national champion and to tech-upgrading goals
Domestic slowdown is real: IP, exports, profits, and urban jobless have deteriorated into early 2019
Yuan and reserves are not in acute distress, so the dispute is costly rather than regime-threatening
April 3 Washington round is live and reporting text-level progress; opponent has not offered a matching tariff rollback
Further Chinese escalation would likely reopen the 10%→25% path; premature purchase/structural giveaways could be pocketed

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
G20 Buenos Aires dinner: 90-day negotiation window; planned Jan 1, 2019 hike of List 3 from 10% to 25% is suspended. Same day: Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou.
US DOJ unseals fraud and sanctions-related charges against Huawei and Meng; US formally requests Meng's extradition from Canada.
Trump tweets that talks have made substantial progress and further delays the scheduled List 3 hike from 10% to 25%.
Intensive Washington talks between US and Chinese negotiators; both sides report progress on text, including enforcement language. No final deal signed.
US imports of goods from China fell from $46.3B (2018-11) to $31.1B (2019-03) / $34.5B (2019-04), about a 25% decline over the window.

Jan–Feb industrial output +5.3% y/y, slowest since early 2002; jobless rate 5.3% in February from 4.9% in December; February exports tumbled the most in three years; official factory PMI contracted in February for first time since January 2009.
Chinese industrial profits suffer sharpest contraction in a decade; trade-war uncertainty and corporate-debt crackdown weaken output.
Kudlow: negotiators making good headway but 'we're not there'; outstanding issues include IP protection and an enforcement mechanism as Liu He meets Lighthizer in Washington.
Stumbling block is Washington's insistence on an enforcement mechanism with penalties; Trump said he wants to keep in place 25 percent taxes on $50 billion of Chinese goods.
